title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is buzzing with partnerships and satellite launches, while budget discussions hint at a growing focus on resilience. Meanwhile, some hypersonic ambitions continue to slip further into the future.

themes.title: Satellite Deployment Surge
themes.body: Qianfan's recent milestone of 200 satellites highlights the rapid growth in LEO constellations. Meanwhile, Amazon's Ariane 6 launch is set to bolster its own satellite ambitions, albeit with some regulatory strings attached.

themes.title: Defense Budget Boost
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to space resilience, indicating a shift in priorities towards safeguarding assets in orbit. This could signal an uptick in contracts for companies focused on space security.

themes.title: Partnerships Flourish
themes.body: Leaf Space's collaboration with D-Orbit and EnduroSat underscores the increasing need for connectivity services in the expanding satellite ecosystem. As companies team up, the landscape is becoming more interconnected, if not more competitive.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hurdles Continue
themes.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle test slipping for the third consecutive quarter raises questions about the pace of U.S. advancements in this area. While the hype around hypersonics persists, tangible progress remains elusive.
